evidence.quote: Quasi-RH?!?!???! Are you kidding me? If a human did this, it would be an instant Fields Medal, no questions asked.

RH says zeta has no zeros in Re(s)>1/2. The best we had until a second ago was a region that got thinner and thinner the higher up the imaginary axis you go. I thought maybe they’d fatten that up a bit, that’d be a massive breakthrough. But no. They got a zero free strip!!!! Insane

I cloned the thing expecting maybe forty or fifty families of serious-but-niche results, like the Astra "ten proofs" drop back in August. Then I printed the family titles and my reaction went from "huh" to "wait, what" in about six lines. Family 003 claims a zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for ζ and every Dirichlet L-function. That's the quasi-Riemann

There are a few caveats. Only around 120 papers have a formalized main result. Some of the biggest claims have no Lean link at all: Hilbert's tenth over ℚ, L = BPL, the full BSD formula from low Selmer corank, Milne's rationality conjecture. The README itself says unformalized results "could have issues," and nobody can referee 700 papers in a couple of
Suddenly, AI has solved 90 of the 500 most important open problems in mathematics

evidence.quote: I've spoken to at least 50+ different groups trying to tokenize some form of yield and getting Yuzu to deploy into it. Making a post on this so it helps those trying to do so to have a better sense of whether they will find success. Also for everyone to have a sense of what we look out for at Yuzu Money. I would caveat by saying that our criteria at Yuzu is

1) Robust. The asset needs have either a long track record showing that it never had any drawdown (or very little). If it doesnt have a long track record it needs to be issued or affiliated by a brand name entity. For e.g. Auto, Home, Prime by Figure.

2) Interest rate sensitivity. Please stop pitching bonds. Bonds have interest rate sensivities. They experience a NAV drawdown when rates go up (aka duration risk). Not to mention the many different intermediary fees. We are in a rate hike cycle. 2Y duration risk looped by 10x = 10% drawdown in 2 rate hikes. This is different from underlying duration of the

3) Liquidity. The asset needs be easily redeemable or unwound. Ideally within a week (e.g. Ethena, Maple, etc). Maximum a month (mGlo by Fasanara). Reason being most of the TVL in DeFi comes from looping. Making your asset loopable is what gets you most of your TVL. See next point.

4) Looping. It must be leveragable on Morpho or Aave. Being leveragable means you are either on Aave v3 or get a major curator (e.g. @SentoraHQ, @gauntlet_xyz, @SteakhouseFi, etc) to green light your asset. Anyone can be on Morpho, but not everyone can pass a good curator's due diligence.

4) Yield. Most of you get this in reverse. You think yield is the most important but it actually is the least. Yield just needs to be higher than 5% (most probably 6%) cause thats what the benchmark (Ethena and Maple) are paying but all of the above is the most important.
